chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the land of Khraj (land tax): if a man buys land from it, builds on it or does not build, and people from the Ahl al-Dhimma (non-Muslims under protection) settle in it, is it permissible for him to take from them the rent of the houses if they pay the Jizyah (poll tax) of their heads? He said: 'He should stipulate terms with them, and whatever he takes from them after the stipulation is halal (permissible).'

key_terms.أَرْضِ الْخَرَاجِ: Khraj land (land subject to land tax)
key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of Dhimma (non-Muslims under protection covenant)

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim own land and rent it to non-Muslims while they pay Jizyah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of a Muslim owning *Khraj* land and leasing it to *Ahl al-Dhimma*, affirming that rent is lawful provided it is based on a clear contractual stipulation (*musharata*). This ruling underscores the principle of *al-istihlak* (acquisition/ownership) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the land's tax status and the private right to lease it. It highlights the flexibility of Islamic property law in accommodating non-Muslim residents while maintaining the owner's right to economic benefit through agreed-upon terms.
